survivors.claim: The catch-all in pictures.js emits a refusal code word `script-error` that appears neither in the header's code list nor in the spec's closed list of eleven codes (Contracts: 'Refusal codes of pictures.js, all exit 2: usage, … send-failed'). Exit code 2 itself is documented, so this is not the hard 'undocumented exit code' case, but a reader of the header cannot learn the twelfth code exists.
survivors.impact: An unexpected crash prints a refusal word no document names, so the person reading it cannot look up what it means.
survivors.evidence: pictures.js:19-21 header lists exactly the eleven codes; pictures.js:256 writes `pictures: script-error — …`. Spec Contracts line 150-151 lists eleven codes. No test or AC exercises the path.

survivors.claim: D1's widths rules (distinct, 1 to 4, integer) and dir rules (trailing slash, `./` prefix, inner `..`) are enforced but pinned by no test: AC-7 covers only `[100]`, `../out`, `/tmp/out`, `.`. The behaviour is correct today (executed above) but is unprotected against regression.
survivors.impact: A later edit could stop refusing duplicate or too-many widths and no test would notice.
survivors.evidence: Executed repro: widths [390,390], [300,400,500,600,700], [], [390.5] each → exit 2 `pictures: bad-config — pictures.widths must be 1 to 4 distinct whole numbers, each 240 to 3840`; dir `design/../design/pictures` → exit 2 bad-config pictures.dir. grep of pictures.test.js shows only the AC-7 literals ([100], ../out, /tmp/out, .) are asserted.
